Weinberger1 Abstract Conﬁdence calibration – the problem of predicting probability estimates representative of the true correctness likelihood – is important for classiﬁcation models in many applications. We discover that modern neural networks, unlike those from a decade ago, are poorly calibrated. Through extensive experiments, we observe that depth, width, weight decay, and Batch Normalization are important factors inﬂuencing calibration.
